name: Era-Tidefall
description: Era-Tidefall is a large, warm oceanic world subjected to extreme tidal forces from its twin moons. The resulting tidal bores are planetary in scale, walls of water hundreds of meters high that sweep across the surface in predictable but devastating cycles.

The dense atmosphere traps heat and moisture, creating a perpetual sauna-like humidity that limits visibility to a few kilometers even on clear days. Thunder rolls constantly from the friction of the massive tides, a low drumbeat that never fully ceases.

The marine fauna that evolved here once thrived in the turbulent waters, adapted to ride the tidal bores across hemispheres. But a gradual shift in the moons' orbits is intensifying the tides beyond historical norms, and the ecosystem is struggling to adapt to the accelerating changes.

Marine biologists consider Era-Tidefall a living laboratory for studying evolutionary pressure in real time. The titanium deposits in the submerged mountain ranges attract mining interests, but extraction in such turbulent waters remains technically challenging and politically contentious.
